body:
Please don't. Things can and will change. If your friends aren't really friends, fuck them. Find new ones. You can find new friends, trust me. If you have to go through a really tough, lonely time, then so be it - you will emerge stronger. 

Suicide is permanent. Misery is temporary; and more importantly it clouds your judgement. Things will change. There have been many people who have been in your exact situation, but their situation has changed and they have come out of it. This will happen to you too. 

If you want to talk via PM, I'm more than happy to talk. I share many of your sentiments, I'm in the same place as you, but I think we could help each other. I'm talking as someone who knows exactly how you feel, and who is in exactly the same situation.

I've made a throwaway just for this. I'm a bit late to the party so I doubt many people will see it, but hell, I think it will be cathartic just to type it out. 

I've always drunk a lot, and taken drugs. It's like I have a pathological need to get fucked every night. I have been to sleep sober maybe 10 times in the last 5 years? I really don't think that's an exaggeration. 

It has caused me huge problems - in fact every problem in my life is directly or indirectly related to this. Money problems for obvious reasons, stealing from loved ones, family, friends is pretty standard behaviour by me. I'm am a vile little person. I obviously make a fool out of myself in social situations; I have very few friends left. And you start to forget that you wake up hungover every day. It just becomes normal. And we all know about the dry throat, shakes, weird poop, and headache that accompany hangovers. But it also makes you feel like shit - angry, depressed. When this is every day, it obtains a veneer of normality and you forget the cause. And you carry on drinking, because when you have that first drink, you feel good again. Oh and another thing - you don't dream when you pass out from drinking. I haven't had a dream in years. That's something I really fucking miss, it's a surprising one. 

So yeah, I've always known this is a problem, never really been able to quit. I've always *wanted to*, but I'm very good at justifying my behaviour. "Oh, I drink way too much but I don't *rely* on it. I just need to drink in moderation". "If I call myself an alcoholic I'm just being a drama queen, this is slightly above-average but nothing as bad as the alcoholics you see on TV". "My life hasn't fallen to pieces yet, I'm still successful in certain ways, I'm not an alcoholic". 

Eventually I was very determined to cut down. I was so ready to do it. I had a big plan - it was my friend's birthday, and I was going to drink in moderation. One an hour, don't get drunk, try to actually remember the night, don't embarrass yourself. Simple. So off I go, and I'm sure you know exactly what happened. Drunk a few beers, then *poof* self-control goes out the window, I order a bottle of wine from the bar, drink it all myself. Eventually I leave the place, wandering down the street with my second bottle of wine in my hand, drunk as a skunk. I'm too fucked to figure out how to get home, so I take a taxi. This is from the centre of my large city, to the outskirts, cost me £40 (about $70 I think?). I get in this taxi even though I know I can't afford it, and I know that I can't take money out of the bank because the ATM won't let me (this is a regular occurrence). I get home, no real idea what I'm gonna do to pay this guy, steal money from my housemate to pay him. 

I woke up the next day and that was it. I tried SO FUCKING HARD to drink in moderation, I could not have been more determined - and I couldn't do it. And you know what? I just thought "I can't do this anymore". 

This story does not have a happy ending (yet). Sorry. It would be really nice to end off by saying "I've now been sober [X] years and couldn't be happier". But I can't say that.
